title: Record IPFS client library selection decision and rationale
description:
## Decision

**Selected: rust-ipfs 0.15.0**

Three candidates were benchmarked. Spike results live in `spikes/` at the repo root.

### iroh-blobs 0.99.0 — DISQUALIFIED

iroh-blobs uses BLAKE3 for content addressing, not SHA-2/CIDv1 multihash. usenet-ipfs requires CIDv1 (SHA-256) for interoperability. No workaround exists. Disqualified regardless of performance.

Benchmarked: p50 add=38.9µs, get=17.6µs (MemStore, 1 KB blocks). See `spikes/iroh-bench/results.md`.

### raw rust-libp2p 0.56.0 + custom bitswap — VIABLE, not selected

p50 ~280µs over loopback TCP (noise + yamux). SHA-2/CIDv1 native. 403 LOC harness for core exchange. Viable but requires the team to own the bitswap codec and want-list/session layers (~500–1500 additional lines) and track the bitswap spec as it evolves. No maintained rust-libp2p bitswap crate exists as of 2026-04. See `spikes/libp2p-bench/results.md`.

### rust-ipfs 0.15.0 — SELECTED

- p50 put=~250ns, get=~930ns (in-memory, 256 distinct 1 KB blocks). 100× faster than loopback alternatives on the hot path.
- SHA-2/CIDv1 native. CIDv1 SHA-256 raw codec out of the box.
- No external daemon. Embedded IPFS node (`DefaultIpfsBuilder`), single binary deploy.
- Includes the libp2p gossipsub and Kademlia stack directly — these are the same primitives usenet-ipfs needs for its overlay. No parallel libp2p stack required.
- Stable Rust (edition 2021), MSRV 1.83. No nightly.
- 466-crate dependency tree, 34 MiB release binary. Large but manageable with `cargo vendor`.

See `spikes/rust-ipfs-bench/results.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] iroh-blobs benchmarked and evaluated (stoa-a2023a88.1.1)
- [x] rust-ipfs benchmarked and evaluated (stoa-a2023a88.1.2)
- [x] raw rust-libp2p benchmarked and evaluated (stoa-a2023a88.1.3)
- [x] Decision recorded with rationale (this issue)
- [x] CLAUDE.md updated to reflect selection
